title: Unions, intersections, and symmetric difference
section: Set Theory ▷ Union and Intersection; Venn Diagrams
terms: union; intersection; disjoint sets; symmetric difference; indexed family; indexed union; indexed intersection; Venn diagram; set De Morgan laws.

exposition.text:
The union A ∪ B uses membership in at least one set, whereas A ∩ B uses membership in both.
Disjoint sets have empty intersection. Symmetric difference A△B = (A \ B) ∪ (B \ A) means
membership in exactly one. Indexed unions use an existential quantifier; indexed intersections
use a universal one.
De Morgan’s laws exchange unions and intersections when taking complements, including in-
finite families. Venn diagrams encode the possible membership patterns and help expose false
identities. Symmetric difference is associative and satisfies A△A = ∅; its behavior matches
addition modulo two of membership indicators. Set difference, in contrast, is not associative.

question.text:
For arbitrary sets A, B, C, which expression equals A \ (B \ C)?
(A) (A \ B) \ C (B) (A \ B) ∪ (A ∩ C)
(C) (A ∩ B) \ C (D) (A ∪ B) ∩ C
(E) A \ (B ∪ C)

solution.text:
c c
An element must lie in A and fail to lie in B ∩ C . De Morgan gives A ∩ (B ∪ C), which
distributes to (A \ B) ∪ (A ∩ C).

question.text:
If A△B = A△C, what must hold?
c
(A) A = ∅ (B) B = C (C) B ∩ C = ∅ (D) A = B = C (E) B = C

solution.text:
Take symmetric difference with A on both sides. Associativity and A△A = ∅ give B = C.
Equivalently, adding the same membership indicator modulo two is cancellative.

question.text:
Finite sets A, B, C have sizes (10, 12, 14), pairwise intersection sizes |A ∩ B| = 4, |A ∩ C| = 5,
|B ∩ C| = 6, and triple intersection size 2. What is |A△B△C|?
(A) 10 (B) 12 (C) 14 (D) 16 (E) 18

solution.text:
Exactly one-set regions contribute 10 − 4 − 5 + 2 = 3, 12 − 4 − 6 + 2 = 4, and 14 − 5 − 6 +
2 = 5 elements. A threefold symmetric difference also includes the two elements in all three

sets. The total is 3 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 14. Equivalently, use |A| − 2 |A ∩ B| + 4|A ∩ B ∩ C|.

question.text:
Which expression describes the shaded region in this Venn diagram?
A B
C
(A) (A \ (B ∪ C)) ∪ ((B ∩ C) \ A) (B) A△B△C
(C) (A ∪ B) \ C (D) (A ∩ B) ∪ C
(E) A \ (B ∩ C)

solution.text:
The left shaded component lies only in A, outside both B and C. The lower-right shaded
component lies in both B and C but outside A. Their union is the expression in A. The
triple intersection is unshaded, unlike a threefold symmetric difference.
